A two-year-old girl died and several people were injured in a multi-vehicle crash on Wednesday. (ABC News)

A two-year-old girl has died after a four-vehicle crash on a major arterial route in inner-city Melbourne this afternoon.

Major Collision Investigation Unit detectives are investigating the incident on Dynon Road, in West Melbourne, just before 4:30pm.

Police said the little girl was in a vehicle being driven by a 30-year-old man, who was taken to hospital with critical injuries.

On Thursday morning, the man was in a stable condition.

Three passengers in the car — a 30-year-old woman, a four-year-old boy and an 11-month-old boy — are in hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the crash on Dynon Road in West Melbourne. (ABC News)

A man, 40, driving a second vehicle was also taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, while a 30-year-old woman driving a third car was treated for minor injuries at the scene by paramedics.

A 62-year-old man who was the sole occupant of a fourth vehicle was also taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

Detectives are still investigating the circumstances of the crash.

Anyone who witnessed the crash, or has information including dashcam footage, should contact Crime Stoppers via 1800 333 000 or www.crimestoppersvic.com.au.
